title: Time-optimal quantum gates with bang-bang control in multilevel systems
authors: Valentín Reparaz, Santiago Ferreyra, María José Sánchez, Daniel Domínguez, Leandro Tosi
abstract: We determine the optimal quantum manipulation protocols for implementing high-fidelity, fast single-qubit gates. We demonstrate that the time-optimal pulse sequence is a ``bang-bang'' sequence: discrete pulses of either positive or negative maximum amplitude or zero. The non-adiabatic bang-bang pulse sequence minimizes gate duration providing a speedup for low-frequency architectures. We first derive the protocol for a transversally driven two-level system, extracting exact analytic expressions for minimum gate times. We then extend this framework to general multilevel architectures, identifying conditions that enable the coherent suppression of leakage errors. Using the fluxonium circuit as a representative case study, we optimize $X/2$ and $Y/2$ gates through a combination of discrete bang sequences and continuous waveform smoothing. This approach preserves near-optimal execution speeds while mitigating transitions outside the computational subspace. Open-system simulations demonstrate that these sequences outperform commensurate and resonant pulse schemes across different fluxonium regimes, achieving low-error manipulation significantly faster than standard resonant control, even in the presence of $1/f$ flux noise and dissipation.
summary: This paper determines the fastest possible way to execute quantum gates by employing time-optimal 'bang-bang' pulse sequences. Using advanced optimal control methods on models like the fluxonium circuit, the authors show these non-adiabatic pulses significantly outperform standard resonant controls in speed and fidelity. This is crucial for scaling up superconducting quantum processors.
main_problem: The primary goal is determining the absolute quantum speed limit for implementing high-fidelity, fast single-qubit gates.
main_result: The time-optimal pulse sequence required to achieve these fast gates is a 'bang-bang' sequence (discrete pulses of maximum amplitude or zero).
method: Optimal Control Theory (OCT) combined with Pontryagin’s Principle was used to derive the necessary control fields, which were then applied to model open system dynamics.
model_or_system: The study models quantum gates on superconducting circuits, initially using a Two-Level System (TLS) and extending to the Fluxonium circuit. The Hamiltonian is controlled by time-dependent external flux $\phi(t)$.
key_observables: Gate fidelity ($F$), minimum gate duration ($t_g$), and leakage rate ($L_1$).
important_parameters: Drive amplitude ($\phi_{	ext{max}}$) relative to the gap ($\Delta$); noise strength ($\sigma$) for $1/f$ flux noise.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that non-adiabatic control sequences are necessary for speedup, and open-system dynamics are modeled using Liouvillian evolution.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate Bloch sphere trajectories comparing resonant vs. time-optimal bang-bang controls; another figure compares minimum gate time versus drive amplitude ratio ($\phi/\Delta$) across different bang structures.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from deriving the optimal control theory for a simple TLS, extending this framework to complex multilevel systems like the fluxonium circuit, and finally simulating the performance under realistic noise models (e.g., $1/f$ flux noise).
why_interesting: This work provides concrete, theoretically derived protocols that push superconducting qubit platforms toward their fundamental speed limits by rigorously applying optimal control theory.
